Subject: Next steps & procurement fit — Redwood options & pricing

Hi Sarah and Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the time and the clear breakdown of Acme's immediate pilot goals and procurement constraints. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of options we discussed
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest to pilot, on-demand billing, no infra lift for you. Good for experimentation and short pilots.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit volumes; requires an onboarding window and contract for reserved capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads where data residency and customer-controlled networking are required.

Commercial tradeoffs
- Commits vs on-demand: commits (12/24 month) reduce unit price but require a spend commitment. On-demand is pay-as-you-go and easiest for pilots.
- Procurement preference matters: PO + Net terms align well with commits and Dedicated purchases; card is common for early pilot spend.

Questions / asks for procurement readiness
1) Which purchase route does finance prefer for pilots: corporate card or PO (Net30/Net45)?
2) Is AWS Marketplace acceptance important to speed procurement?
3) Who is the procurement/legal contact on your side (name + email) to loop in for contract/PO steps?
4) Rough expected pilot spend and timeline (helps us size Dedicated vs Hosted recommendations).

Files attached: redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf (high-level bands), redwood-mpo-summary.xlsx (marketplace onboarding notes).

Suggested next step: if procurement signals PO + Net30, we can prepare a short SOW + packet for legal and a Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison tailored to the pilot. Happy to run a 30-minute procurement/finance alignment call this week.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez

Hi Sarah — thanks, very helpful. Short answers and next steps below.

PO / Billing
- We accept PO with Net30 by default for enterprise customers (we can support Net45 on request; exceptions require approval). We invoice monthly for on-demand usage or as per the reserved capacity schedule for committed contracts.
- ACH is supported.
- AWS Marketplace: we can onboard there; it accelerates procurement for some customers but has separate billing mechanics (marketplace fees and lead time to activate listing).

Dedicated vs Hosted (recommendation for Acme pilot)
- Pilot recommendation: start on Hosted (Redwood API, on-demand). Low friction, gets you to results in days.
- If pilot throughput grows and you need predictable per-token cost, move to Dedicated with a 6-12 month reserved commitment — we'll produce an estimate showing cost parity point.
- Private deployment is an option if you need a dedicated VPC or specific compliance controls, but it's typically a later-stage decision and involves longer setup.

Attachments: I attached an Acme-specific hosting comparison (acme-hosting-comparison.csv) that maps expected pilot volume to cost and onboarding time. Laura is cc'd and will follow up on contract language and the PO workflow.

Next steps
1) Sarah — can you share the procurement contact (email + best time window) so Laura can send the contract packet and a short SOW?
2) If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute procurement sync (Laura + Monica + your procurement lead) to walk through billing options and marketplace tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Mateo

Hi Sarah — Laura here from Contracts. Keeping this short:

1) We have a standard commercial agreement that covers Hosted and Dedicated purchase flows; Dedicated addenda for reserved capacity only add a few clauses around commit volumes and termination economics. No unusual data-handling language is required by default; we can add a short data-processing addendum if Acme wants more explicit terms.

2) To get a PO over the finish line, please send the procurement contact and any internal reference numbers (SOW id, PO template). We'll produce a contract packet and a redlineable PDF.

3) If you plan to purchase via AWS Marketplace, legal review is usually faster but marketplace invoicing will be handled by the marketplace partner. Let us know which path you prefer and we'll tailor the packet.

I can join a 30-minute sync next week. Mateo — I'll draft the packet and include a contract stub (redwood-contract-stub.pdf).
